quote: you guys are, like, the folks that my neighbor used used
stewart_read: Unsolicited social proof handed to the rep at the start of the call — a strong trust anchor.
coaching_implication: Rep chased the neighbor's name once then dropped it; should have captured it and referenced it again at button-up to reinforce trust ('like we did for your neighbor on Trillium').

stewart_read: Rep asks the right follow-up but the thread is abandoned mid-conversation when the customer's audio cuts out, and never revisited.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: rep got knocked off track by the audio glitch and simply moved into verify.
coaching_implication: Even after the interruption, rep could have circled back once things stabilized to capture the referral name for the file and use it as rapport leverage.

stewart_read: Bill/kWh usage captured but the rep moves directly to the next data point (verifying prior month) with no emotional acknowledgment.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: rep may have been optimizing for speed given customer was mid-login and slightly distracted, prioritizing efficient data capture over rapport.
coaching_implication: A one-line flip such as 'that adds up fast over a year' would have anchored the pain before pivoting to scheduling.

quote: you have to do it in site inspection?
stewart_read: Customer's logistics question is really a soft legitimacy/commitment check before agreeing to the appointment.
coaching_implication: Handled adequately in the moment; rep answered concretely with the phone-call alternative.

quote: Yeah. What's interested you in solar for your home?

coaching_implication: Without this, the rep has no stated 'why' to tie the appointment or the bill pain to; this is the single biggest content gap in the call.
